questions.q: After Solomon finished building the house of Yahweh, what did Yahweh do?
questions.a: When Solomon finished the house of Yahweh, he appeared to Solomon a second time.

questions.q: What did Yahweh say to Solomon?
questions.a: Yahweh said to Solomon, “I have heard your prayer and request you made before me.”

questions.q: What did Yahweh want Solomon to obey?
questions.a: Yahweh wanted Solomon to obey all the commandments and decrees that he had commanded him.

questions.q: What did Yahweh promise to David, Solomon’s father?
questions.a: Yahweh promised to establish the throne of David’s kingdom over Israel forever.

questions.q: What did Yahweh tell Solomon he would do if Solomon did not keep his commandments?
questions.a: Yahweh told Solomon that he would cut off Israel from the ground that he had given them.

questions.q: What would people ask when they passed by the temple of Yahweh?
questions.a: People would ask, “Why has Yahweh done this to this land and to this house?”

questions.q: Why would Yahweh bring this disaster on them?
questions.a: Yahweh would bring disaster on them because they abandoned their God and worshiped other gods.

questions.q: What happened at the end of 20 years?
questions.a: At the end of 20 years, Solomon finished building the temple of Yahweh and the king’s palace.

questions.q: With what did Hiram king of Tyre furnish Solomon?
questions.a: Hiram king of Tyre furnished Solomon with cedar trees, cypress trees, and gold.

questions.q: What did Hiram come from Tyre to see?
questions.a: Hiram came from Tyre to see the cities that Solomon had given him.

questions.q: What did Hiram call the cities which Solomon had given him?
questions.a: Hiram called the cites the land of Cabul, which means worthless.

questions.q: How much gold did Hiram send to king Solomon?
questions.a: Hiram had sent 120 kikkars of gold to the king.

questions.q: What did Solomon have built at Hazor, Megiddo, and Gezer?
questions.a: Solomon had cities built at Hazor, Megiddo, and Gezer.

questions.q: What did Pharaoh king of Egypt do at Gezer?
questions.a: Pharaoh king of Egypt took Gezer and burned it, and also killed the Canaanites in the city.

questions.q: What did Solomon do at Gezer and Beth Horon?
questions.a: Solomon rebuilt Gezer and Beth Horon.

questions.q: What did Solomon do with the people in the land who were not of Israel?
questions.a: The people in the land who were not of Israel Solomon made into forced laborers.

questions.q: What did Solomon do with the people of Israel?
questions.a: Solomon made the people of Israel become soldiers, servants, officials, officers and commanders.

questions.q: How many chief officers did Solomon have?
questions.a: Solomon had 550 chief officers who were over the supervisors.

questions.q: What did Solomon offer three times a year?
questions.a: Solomon offered burnt offerings and peace offerings on the altar of Yahweh three times a year.

questions.q: What did Solomon do at Ezion Geber?
questions.a: Solomon built a fleet of ships at Ezion Geber.

questions.q: Why did Solomon send servants to Ophir?
questions.a: Solomon sent servants to Ophir to bring back gold.

commentary.text: The presents of Solomon and Hiram.

Verses 1–9 God warned Solomon, now he had newly built and dedicated the temple, that he and his people might not be high-minded, but fear. After all the services we can perform, we stand upon the same terms with the Lord as before. Nothing can purchase for us liberty to sin, nor would the true believer desire such a licence. He would rather be chastened of the Lord, than be allowed to go on with ease and prosperity in sin.

Solomon gave Hiram twenty cities. Hiram did not like them. If Solomon would gratify him, let it be in his own element, by becoming his partner in trade, as he did. See how the providence of God suits this earth to the various tempers of men, and the dispositions of men to the earth, and all for the good of mankind in general.

Here is a further account of Solomon's greatness. He began at the right end, for he built God's house first, and finished that before he began his own; then God blessed him, and he prospered in all his other buildings. Let piety begin, and profit follow; leave pleasure to the last. Whatever pains we take for the glory of God, and to profit others, we are likely to have the advantage. Canaan, the holy land, the glory of all lands, had no gold in it; which shows that the best produce is that which is for the present support of life, our own and others; such things did Canaan produce. Solomon got much by his merchandise, and yet has directed us to a better trade, within reach of the poorest. Wisdom is better than the merchandise of silver, and the gain thereof than fine gold, Pr 3:14.
